title: Town Hall Open-Mic Plan + Q&A Scratchpad
content:
Notes to self — raw and fragmented. Goal: build an open-mic segment after the CEO update to increase cross-team visibility and surface friction points. This is not polished.

Purpose:
- Give engineers/product folks short public mic time (2–3 minutes) to demo a live win or ask for help.
- Let leadership hear raw signals without filtering.
- Keep it lightweight and low-ceremony so people are more likely to volunteer.

Constraints / guardrails:
- 10 slots, 3 minutes each + 1 moderator (engineering host). Total ~40 minutes including transitions.
- Prioritize product/infra topics that affect multiple teams (latency regressions, deploy config, billing UX, Dedicated capacity issues).
- No sales/customer pitches. If customer-focused, must be framed as learnings/asks.

Run of show (first draft):
- 0:00–0:05 — Welcome, safety + net (recording on/off), code of conduct quick note (Lena)
- 0:05–0:25 — Leadership updates (CEO 7m, CTO 7m — condensed)
- 0:25–0:40 — Town Hall Open Mic slots (moderated)
- 0:40–0:50 — Live Q&A panel (CEO/CTO/Head of Product)
- 0:50–1:00 — Wrap and CTAs (ops triage channels + follow-ups)

How to recruit volunteers (channels):
- Short signup doc (Google form) + ask folks to paste 1–2 sentence blurb. Link: placeholder form.
- Encourage demos that include: 1-line problem, 1-line impact (#users/cost/latency), 1 ask (help/request).
- Slack nudge cadence: T-7d, T-3d, T-1d. Use #all-company and team channels.

Moderator script (bullets):
- "Thanks — name, team, 2-sentence setup, 1 ask. Timer set to 3 minutes. No slides."
- Use a visible timer; call out when 30s remain.
- If overheated topics (policy/legal/security), flag for follow-up with relevant owner instead of live debate.

Sample slot blurb templates for volunteers:
- "Hi, I'm Alex (Serving Runtime). We saw a 10% latency spike on p95 after last kernel change; impacts 2 large customers. Current ask: anyone with e2e repro or telemetry expertise to sync after town hall."
- "Hi, I'm Noor (Product). We're validating dedicated autoscale patterns — looking for customers to pilot; want to talk to platform teams who run long-tail inference workloads."

Planned leadership talking points to prep (notes):
- CEO: macro, business health, ARR growth signal (high level), hiring posture
- CTO: stability/capacity: 99.95% target vs actual this quarter, plan for Dedicated capacity expansion, early notes on private deployments onboarding friction
- Engineering head: highlight two wins (KV cache improvement landed, batching improvements decreased token cost by X%) and one open technical debt request (observability long-tail traces)

Metrics to surface (grab from product analytics and infra):
- Hosted API: median latency (ms) / p95 / error rate (last 30d vs prior)
- Dedicated: avg utilization vs committed capacity
- Private: onboarding time (days) and blocker list
- Cost: $/M tokens baseline + top 3 optimization wins this quarter

Anticipated tough questions + seed answers (draft):
- Q: "Why did latency spike last week?"
  A: short: deployed kernel change to optimize memory; regression surfaced at tail due to batch scheduling; mitigation: rolled back, working on scheduling fix. Follow-up: postmortem doc link.
- Q: "Any plan to support [specific GPU type]?"
  A: We have experimental builds; prioritization tied to Dedicated tenant demand — if you have customer asks, escalate to Solutions Eng (link)
- Q: "How are we controlling costs for hosted free-tier?"
  A: We use intelligent batching & caching heuristics tiered by customer segment; plan to add quota guardrails and automated warm caches for free-tier to prevent abuse.

Open items / TODO:
- [ ] Finalize volunteer signup form and embed in calendar invite (Due: 2026-03-01) — Diego
- [ ] Get CTO confirmation on the two metric numbers (p95 and Dedicated utilization) — Priya
- [ ] Draft 1-paragraph on Private onboarding friction for CTO to read — Lena
- [ ] Confirm recording policy + captions (People Ops) — ping Ruby
- [ ] Arrange visible timer tool (Zoom shared app or OBS overlay) — engineering infra owner

Housekeeping + follow-ups after town hall:
- Capture all asks into JIRA board COMM-TOWNHALL and assign owners. Template for slot: summary, impact, ask, owner, triage by PM/Eng lead.
- Send TL;DR email with 3 bullets and links to artifacts within 24 hours
- 1-week follow-up note in #all-company with progress on top 3 asks

Risks and friction:
- Open-mic could surface untriaged public criticism; need moderation and rapid private follow-up to avoid public blame cycles.
- Time overruns. Mitigation: strict timer + pre-screen volunteers if >10 signups.
- Security-sensitive info leaks. Moderator to flag and hand to security channel.

Questions I still have / decisions to make:
- Should we require volunteers to pre-submit a 1-slide artifact? Pros: keeps things focused. Cons: reduces spontaneity.
- Will leadership be comfortable with a wide-open mic where some topics might be crunchy (deploys, outages)? Need to ask CEO/CTO.
- Does People Ops want a small panel for recognition (Velvet awards) during same hour? Probably scope creep.

Slack links & resources (placeholders):
- Signup form: https://forms.gle/townhall-open-mic
- Confluence draft page: https://confluence.redwood/townhall/open-mic-draft
- JIRA triage board: https://jira.redwood/browse/COMM
- Slack prep thread: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C0123ABC

Notes to self (voice):
- Keep it low friction. The win is when someone in infra says "that problem's been bothering us for months" and five people offer quick syncs.
- Don't try to solve everything live — capture and assign.

End of scratchpad. Will prune, then share with Diego and Priya for next-week dry run.
